idiom_name: JetStream ObjectStore: PutBytes/Put with an object name as the claim check
implementation_notes: Go has no claim-check component, but the store half has a first-class implementation: a JetStream ObjectStore created with js.CreateObjectStore chunks an object over an ordinary stream and returns ObjectInfo whose Name is the claim check, with PutBytes/PutString/PutFile to write and Get/GetBytes to read it back. The seam stays application code - marshal an envelope carrying the object name, publish it on the small subject, redeem it in the consumer before processing - which is what separates this from the framework-level realizations in Java or .NET. Within one process the payload need not be stored at all: hand over an *os.File or io.ReadCloser (a live handle) or a temp path instead of bytes, and prefer the ObjectStore form whenever the payload must survive a consumer restart, because handles and temp files do not.
code_sketch:
obj, err := js.CreateObjectStore(ctx, jetstream.ObjectStoreConfig{Bucket: "payloads"})
info, err := obj.PutBytes(ctx, "orders/4471", payload)   // chunked over a stream
env, err := json.Marshal(Envelope{OrderID: id, ClaimCheck: info.Name})
nc.Publish("orders.new", env)                             // only the reference travels
// consumer: rc, err := obj.Get(ctx, msg.ClaimCheck); defer rc.Close(); io.ReadAll(rc)
pitfalls: The object name is the whole security boundary: anyone who can publish the reference can hand one out, and anyone who can guess or observe a name can fetch it, so names must be unguessable and the bucket must carry its own permissions.

Get returns a reader that owns resources and objects are chunked into the stream: forgetting to close leaks subscriptions, and Delete only writes a delete marker, so space is reclaimed by the stream's own limits rather than immediately.
Object stores require nats-server 2.9.0 or newer, and the failure is a runtime error rather than a compile-time one.
PutBytes copies the whole payload into memory; use Put with a reader (or PutFile) for payloads that should stream in chunks.
